segments.text: Will you choose to bring a child into this world?
Teaching a child is hard
Raising one is even harder
If they’re going to suffer after being born
They won’t have to suffer if they aren’t born
But they won’t experience joy either
I think love is very important
How deep is a mother’s love?
When your wife went for IVF
she had to undergo 300 to 400 injections
Yes
You know the nursery song
There Is Nothing Like a Mother’s Love
It’s true
It’s a very complicated feeling
Love makes everything worth it
My eldest was sitting here
my second eldest over here
and my third eldest on my lap
I asked them if we should get a car
They said no
because they won’t get to sit like this
Elon Musk said
that Singapore and many other countries are facing extinction
It sounds like an exaggeration
but in reality
Singapore’s total fertility rate has dropped to 0.87
In other words
most people may never have a child in their lifetime
The Government has called this
Singapore’s existential crisis
Interestingly, we seem to be the exception here
The four of us have 14 kids in total
That’s enough to form a soccer team
with three substitutes
But among us
Lo Hok Him has chosen not to have kids
Hok Him is 42
Yes
Our second guest is James Kwan Chee Haw
Our third guest is
Michael See Chern Siong, a secondary school teacher
Elon Musk said that Singapore is going extinct
When you heard that
how did you react?
He’s right
Our total fertility rate is too low
Hok Him, you decided not to have kids
What led you to the decision?
Teaching a child is hard
raising one is even harder
I wanted my wife and I to have an easier life
I know it’s a little selfish of me
How about James?
All of us have to work harder
and learn from our buddy here
That’s how we can save Singapore
Michael, what do you think about Elon’s comment?
I never intended to have eight kids
Our first attempt resulted in a miscarriage
My wife suffered depression for five to six months
She could still take it
After that she developed Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
That really hit us hard
I thought God was messing with me
The doctor told us
we may not be able to have kids
without medical intervention
How did you survive the ordeal?
Through prayer
My friends told us it’s okay
We may not become parents
but we are still husband and wife
We were husband and wife first anyway
We stopped worrying
and decided to leave it to God
We decided not to go for IVF
or any medical intervention
That was the principle we stood by
Since I was young
I’ve seen many relatives and friends
who suffered miscarriages
It’s hard for them to move on from the grief
When we also reached that age
the chances of miscarriage went up
I didn’t want my wife to suffer the same pain
I know my wife
I really didn’t want her to go through that
When we reached our late 30s
we thought this might be our last chance
we did see a specialist
to learn more
and give us some kind of closure
That was when my wife and I came to a decision
We decided we won’t have kids
I know you’re the only son in the family
Yes
Chinese families usually have certain expectations
To pass on the family line
How did you convince your family?
I have some older relatives who think this way
But those closest to me, like my mother
don’t share those views
Since I was a kid she has always
let us do what we wanted
To her
she’s happy as long as I’m happy
To me
if I were to have a kid
I’ll have to slog for
that one kid or few kids
I won’t get to live as comfortably as I can
I don’t think my mother wants that
So, they don’t talk about it?
No, they never talk about it
I don’t see kids as some kind of insurance policy
or a way to continue the family line
My wife and I don’t expect our kids to take care of us
Since they were kids, I’ve told them
I don’t need monthly allowance or outings
We can take care of ourselves
When it’s just the two of us
we can do whatever we want
But when a kid comes into the picture
you have to care for it
It’s a huge change
but after the first kid
taking care of the rest are easier
Why
They’re all around the same age
They will watch out for and take care of each other
They’ll play and grow up together
Keep it up and have a few more kids
But he’s right
With more kids
they can take care of each other
My kid started doing chores at one
They can sort and fold the laundry
If they drop food
they’ll pick it up themselves
That’s great, because they become more careful
They fold their own clothes
and clean up after themselves
That’s because you spent time teaching them
That’s how they learned
They’re not born knowing all that
You’ve invested a lot of time and effort in that
When we had our first kid
we weren’t expecting a second kid
We decided to teach her how to take care of herself
When the second kid came along
the first taught the second
It’s like a domino effect
The first teaches the second
No, it’s because the first wanted to retire
When the 8th kid came along
she didn’t have to do anything
The eldest wanted to retire
so she had to teach the second
She can only retire after that
The management
makes sure everything’s being done right
James, when you decided to have a third child
did you expect it to be so hard?
We had an easy time with our first two kids
My wife got pregnant
in the month we first started trying
That’s impressive
Not too bad
But when we tried for our third
things got strange
We just can’t seem to conceive
We started to go for checkups
Apparently, the quality of my sperm dropped
I thought, is this my issue?
So, I took some supplements
to boost the quality of my sperm
But that didn’t work
That was the first year
My wife got pregnant
but she miscarried
There was a lot of guilt and self-reproach going around
As men
we think there’s always time
We’re still young
and have plenty of chances
At first, I thought it was because of me
Later, we found out it wasn’t
My wife had a Caesarean Scar Defect
and needed surgery
to conceive a third child
When the doctor told you
You can try
but you’ll need to undergo a surgery
Did you hesitate?
Yes. I was also very afraid
My father had a surgery too
It was successful
but he still passed
It affected my confidence in surgeries
The surgeon who operated on my father
was a really famous surgeon
He told us
the surgery had a 95% success rate
Even with a 95% success rate
my father still passed away
So that got me thinking
The surgery wasn’t that straightforward too
What if something was to happen to my wife?
We deliberated over the matter for very long
Did your wife make the final decision?
Even if she decides against having kids
she still had to do something about her CSD
An accidental bump or injury
might cause the scar to rupture and kill her
Regardless whether we wanted kids
she had to get the surgery done
How well did she handle that?
All she could think about was the kids
She didn’t look worried
but when she entered the operating theatre
she realised
what if something were to happen to her?
What will happen to her two kids and husband?
What about her parents?
That was when she broke down
How did she break down?
She started crying in the operating room
The medical staff had to calm her down
When your wife went for IVF
She had to endure the pain of 300 to 400 injections, right?
Yes
You had to give her a quarter of those injections
How did you feel?
You know the nursery song?
There Is Nothing Like a Mother’s Love
It’s true
That’s how I felt
When I helped my wife with the injections
I was so nervous
You’re supposed to cherish your wife
not cause her pain
Now, I have to give her an injection everyday
You have an excuse now
No
It just feels weird
You’re supposed to love your wife
but now you have to hurt her
It’s a very complicated feeling
I was lucky
Your story really moved me
Our first few years were difficult
but after that, we had no trouble conceiving
All our kids were conceived
and delivered through natural birth
Her first delivery took 20 minutes
She’s saving cost for you
She said she’s saved so much for us
That’s the most painful experience a woman can have
She didn’t even take any epidural for her first birth
No painkillers and the baby was born, just like that
She said if she can do it once
she can do it again
I was the one who delivered our last baby
We were just outside KK Women's and Children's Hospital
We had the delivery in the car
You couldn’t get to the hospital in time
We couldn’t
That’s why it’s memorable for you
Yes, I cried at every delivery
I was there with her
I was the one who cut the umbilical cord
That’s why I told my wife
we’re in this together
You’re not raising the kids alone
We’re doing it together
Hok Him is the youngest of us all
He’s a millennial
The current US-Iran conflict
Russia-Ukraine war
and the COVID-19 pandemic
all happened during your time
Some call you guys the unluckiest generation
What do you think?
From my perspective
the year I graduated from university
Lehman Brothers collapsed
Finding a job that year was really hard
I studied engineering
I heard that
in the past, if you earn the 1st class honours
you can expect a certain salary
That all flew out the window
Many people said
by starting out with a lower salary
over the course of your career
it brings down the salary you earn
You’ve gone through a lot
Did that affect your decision
to not have children?
I believe that my life experiences
do affect my decision-making to a certain degree
I feel that many things in life are very stressful
and life itself is tough
You have to keep slogging
If I have a child
I would love them dearly
If they’re going to suffer after being born
I wouldn’t want that
I would rather not have them
They won’t have to suffer if they aren’t born
But they won’t experience joy either
There is no absolute
You never know what kind of life they’ll have
Maybe they will live a happy life
And their parents may share that happiness
As long as you can make them feel loved
They must know that their parents love them
When my kids get their PSLE results
they said, Mom, Dad,
it doesn’t matter what grades we get
you still love us, right?
I said, Right
the most important thing is to do your best
As parents, we want to give our everything to our children
But the hardship that kids face
Like being bullied in school
or facing problems in looking for jobs
or facing relationship issues
even getting scolded by their bosses
That’s too much
I don’t want my child to have to go through that
That’s how a father feels
I’ve lived that
My kid is working part-time now
She’s been through that
Getting scolded by her boss and customers
Getting scolded for getting bad grades
getting bullied
What’s important is how they overcome that
How are you going to improve your grades?
How do you deal with your bullies?
As a parent, being there for your child matters too
Many say that raising kids is unprofitable
What do you think?
Do you agree?
No, because basically
you're seeing it from a financial angle
That’s not the right way of looking at this
Raising kids can’t be measured in monetary terms
No
How much is your parents’ love worth?
Nothing or priceless?
You need money to raise kids
but you don’t need a lot
There are subsidies for education
and healthcare
They always ask the same questions
Does your child attend enrichment classes?
How about tuition?
How about this and that?
When you hear them
you wonder who’s asking for those?
Them or their kids?
The kids end up exhausted every weekend
They have no time to talk to you
Who’s the one to blame?
Our kids or our own expectations?
Someone did the math. Raising a child
from birth to the age of 30 will cost a million
A million
My wife and I did our own math
If that’s true, we would be finished
We don’t agree with that
The kids have hand-me-downs
They don’t attend tuition
I find that unnecessary
If they want to pick up guitar or piano
they can do that as adults
and they’ll be more interested
They can even learn from YouTube
The biggest expenses
are healthcare costs
Many people may think
for families with a lot of kids
the kids may miss out on a lot of things
Do you feel that way?
If you talk to my kids
and ask them if they’re missing out if they don’t travel
they would say no
they don’t think so
Are they missing out if we don’t own a car?
No
My three eldest daughters
When we took the MRT for the first time
my eldest was sitting here
my second eldest over here
my third eldest on my lap
I asked them if we should get a car
They said no
because they won’t get to sit like this
I couldn’t afford a car anyway
I was just asking
It depends on what you want
If you think you need your kid to get all As
You need them to get a scholarship to make you proud
You need them to get AL4 for PSLE
and attend enrichment classes
I think you should reconsider if you really want a kid
I’m really moved by what he said
If I were him
I would be touched too
But to me
I’ll keep asking myself
if I’ve done enough for them
Can I do more?
If I have a kid
I think I’ll be very stressed
I want to give them everything
Without kids, I won’t have that stress
My kids have been volunteering with me since young
They started volunteering at the ages of 3 to 4
We distribute rice to those poor families
They used to think we don’t have much
When they visited a 1-room flat
they were so shocked
They don’t even have air-conditioning
They have to share a common fan
and they eat on the floor, not on the table
So, they were content with what they have
A lot of the time, we don’t see what we have
only what we don’t have
Visiting those families
It changed their mindsets
It changed them completely
They never asked for their own handphones
Like he said, we want to give our kids the best
That’s our view
But what does your child want most from you?
Is it money?
No
Is it time with you
Yes
It’s your love
Love and time
That’s what they want
The Government wants to change
our mindset on seeing parenthood as a net loss
and reduce our stress of being the perfect parent
That way, we may have more kids
What is the one measure that is critical
and should be implemented right away?
I don’t get that much subsidies
I pay a lot more
When bus fares rise by one cent
I pay $2 more for the whole family
My utility fees cost more too
I have ten people in my household
so we use a lot of water
The more you use, the more you are penalised
If you want us to have more children
you need to think of our needs
Each household gets $500 worth of CDC vouchers
I use that up in two trips
If I can’t ensure a better life for my next generation
I would feel like I’ve failed them
Singapore must ensure our next generation
gets the same opportunities
During my time, while I was still growing up
Singapore was still developing
and we had a lot of opportunities
But competition is tough now
and I worry about that
If we can resolve this
so that I know for sure that
if the next generation is willing to put in the work
they will lead better lives than my generation
at least for me
I can have kids with a greater peace of mind
On average
you need to undergo IVF three times to conceive
I encourage women to freeze their eggs
because both egg quality and quantity
after 35, decline significantly
Allow them to use their MediSave to pay for the procedure
Elon only cared about the figure 0.87
But to many people
raising a child isn’t about figures
Children are a heritage given to us
and as parents, we must manage them well
As for those who choose not to bear kids
we must respect their decision
and wish them a lifetime of love together
What do you choose?
Leave us your comments below
Thank you for joining us today
